items.text: ← and → turn a dial when it has focus, instead of also changing scene (Autoplay's Every dial too)

Follows and Adjust are drawers in the color editor: Follows shows its tie on its button and opens across the whole editor, both rows seen whole with nothing to scroll; Adjust holds this color's lightness, chroma and hue; the "one ground" and "one ink" buttons are gone (clear the slot on the strip)
the ground line's counts are one dial (drag round, as Autoplay's Every), so the line is short and the dice is never cut off; every bead's dots sit under it
every line in What's new says what it is (new, fix or change); some of today's did not

the mix is a bead: between Ink 1 and Ink 2 on the strip, a round bead on the thread that ties them; a tap steps grain, speed, tempo, and its dots say which. The same between the two grounds: gradient or turns. How each mixes is in the info drawer

the two grounds are one line of beads, like Autoplay's Every: Ground 1 · mix · Ground 2 · direction (a tap turns it) · hand, beats or bars · how many · the dice. By hand you choose which ground shows; with a count the gradient turns, or the grounds swap, on the tempo; the dice picks a new length and a new direction each time
a color dragged onto an empty slot (Arrows or Pattern hidden, no Ink 2, no Ground 2) now takes, and brings it back on. Every empty swatch shows the same diagonal lines (Ground 2's X is gone)
Follows, seen: free or a color by name, then how, each way a swatch already showing the color it would give, its name underneath. No more long list

for long shows: a scene with picture moves no longer adds a copy each visit; the library is written at most once a second; a stopped bytebeat costs nothing; a video or camera driving the field reuses one canvas; a recording left on stops growing after two and a half minutes, and a full browser storage now says so
the list of palettes under a palette's name no longer covers the Color panel's band (‹ ›, the ring, close): it takes the editor's place inside the panel and scrolls there
a scene keeps its rain: save a scene with a fill on and it comes back on a dry floor every time, and the rain fills it again (over bars, with sound or your finger, and how many bars)

rain fills the pool, a Water setting under Surface (fill). Seen from above, the first drops land on a dry hard floor and splash wide, leaving beads of water everywhere; more and more rain falls, puddles open in the floor's hollows and join, and when the whole surface is water the surface you picked takes over with its waves. Fill it over bars (8, 16, 32 or 64, on the tempo), with sound (it rains as loud as the sound is), or with your finger (it rains where you touch). Dry again starts over
a panel whose contents settle a moment after it opens (the microphone's) glides to its height once, instead of twice
stepping into the Color editor or between its views glides once too; the two animations no longer fight over one height
the panel titles all sit in one place and one size: Field is no longer larger, Color palettes no longer indented, and the Color panel's editor says Editor at the top
Sequences are Pro, open to everyone while in beta: the open padlock on the Sequence title

the show lock. While a sequence plays, Lock (or Shift+L) leaves only ‹ › and the robot: no panel, drawer, ring or other key can open by accident, and the screen stays awake. It lasts through a reload. A small lock shows top left; hold it for a second (or Shift+L) to unlock
in a sequence, duplicate and remove are buttons on each entry, and a grip on the right drags it to a new place (or arrow keys on the grip)
Follows has its own line in the color editor, so its choice reads whole ("complement of Ink 1")
every scroll bar follows the light or dark chrome, not only the Color panel's
a sequence's scene pictures are bigger, as tall as the entry's name and its settings together
